pending_commit.commit_message: cr50: use dedicated region for info1 accesses The INFO1 flash space is used for various purposes (endorsement key seed, Board ID and flags, serial number, etc.). Accessing these spaces in INFO1 is accompanied by managing the flash region registers, each time opening a window of the appropriate size, with appropriate permissions, etc, In fact none of these spaces contain a secret, to simplify things and preventing situations when concurrent accesses change the flash range window settings lets dedicate previously unused Region 7 register file to providing always open read access to INFO1. Write access will be enabled/disabled as required. In prod images write accesses will always happen from the vendor command context. In DBG images CLI commands will also have write access to INFO1. INFO1 window is accessed by other H1 based devices as well, this is why it is necessary to enable the window in the common chip code. vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. dlcservice: Maintain cache state of dlc roots Dlcservice will maintain the dlc roots alongside the installed DLC(s). During |LoadDlcModuleImages()|, it is already the case that if a mounting fails then the failed DLC will not end up in |installed_dlc_modules_|, so |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will only add to the |installed_dlc_modules_| DLC(s) that are installed with mount. During |Install()|, no change is made to |installed_dlc_modules_|. During |Uninstall()|, we only remove from |installed_dlc_modules_| if unmounting and deleting both succeed (neither unmount nor delete should ever fail, but in the case that they do, it will lead dlcservice into an unstable state). Deleting al already deleted file or directory returns true and will not fail, which desired behavior. During |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| most of the work happens. Dlcservice goes through the DLC(s) that finished installing and need to be mounted. Only when all the `to be` installed DLC(s) are mounted, do they go into the |installed_dlc_modules_| with there corresponding dlc roots. net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. This change introduces exponential backoff so that if an empty response is received from the printer, ippusbxd will wait for increasingly long periods before issuing another request. This change significantly reduces syslog spam, and should result in faster communication with the printer. vm_tools: Put ARCVM processes in a proper cpu cgroup This CL bind-mounts host's |session_manager_container| cpu cgroup into Concierge. The cgroup is for Chrome to throttle Android processes (both ARC++ and ARCVM) based on its active window state etc. The CL also modifies Concierge's ARCVM code so that it adds ARCVM's crosvm process to |session_manager_container| group right after fork() but before execve(). With that, the first crosvm process and all its children will belong to the right cpu cgroup instead of the default one, /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/vms. Alternatives considered: Move ARCVM's crosvm process(es) somewhere outside Concierge. => This doesn't work well because the PID of crosvm Concierge knows is for Concierge's own PID namespace. The PID is useless outside Concierge, and the outside process in the init PID namespace has to scan through /proc/<pid> entries to find the crosvm process. Also, crosvm spawns threads and child processes after it's executed. Moving all of them without introducing races is a messy job. OTOH, if we change the crosvm's cpu cgroup before execve() (which is what this CL does), we don't have the race issue. BUG=b:135608119 TEST=Start arcvm, observe both /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/vms/tasks and /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/session_manager_containers/tasks, verify all ARCVM crosvm processes are in the latter group. UPSTREAM: mm: don't cap request size based on read-ahead setting We ran into a funky issue, where someone doing 256K buffered reads saw 128K requests at the device level. Turns out it is read-ahead capping the request size, since we use 128K as the default setting. This doesn't make a lot of sense - if someone is issuing 256K reads, they should see 256K reads, regardless of the read-ahead setting, if the underlying device can support a 256K read in a single command. This patch introduces a bdi hint, io_pages. This is the soft max IO size for the lower level, I've hooked it up to the bdev settings here. Read-ahead is modified to issue the maximum of the user request size, and the read-ahead max size, but capped to the max request size on the device side. The latter is done to avoid reading ahead too much, if the application asks for a huge read. With this patch, the kernel behaves like the application expects. shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. This adds about 30k to the binary size but rust binaries will no longer depend on gcc_s. This change required an upstream patch to make it build with cross-compilation. The libunwind code was missing from from the llvm fork shipped with the rustc source tarball for unknown reasons. The ebuild sources the llvm fork directly from github and places the libunwind source in the correct spot. Because gcc_s isn't linked, a latent bug in mosys's link step was seen on armv7 builds. There was a missing compiler builtin that gcc_s provided that is no longer there. This was fixed in this CL by including the default libs via `-C default-linker-libraries`, which pulls in LLVM's compiler_rt. See crbug.com/868726 for more details about the issue.
